summary.headline: INOX India Q1 FY27 order inflow hit a record ~INR532 crore, lifting order book to ~INR1,686 crore; revenue of INR382 crore grew ~8.3% YoY, below management's own INR410-415 crore target.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 total income was INR382 crore (+8.3% YoY) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+1.4% YoY, 23.5% margin), with PAT flat at INR61 crore. Management attributed the revenue shortfall to INR32-35 crore of equipment ready for dispatch but held back due to freight rate spikes and ship availability issues. Order inflow was a record ~INR532 crore, driven by a large US space-sector cryogenic tank order, with the order book at INR1,686 crore, of which over INR1,140 crore is export. Management reiterated 18-20% FY27 revenue growth guidance and a 21-24% EBITDA margin range.

segments.name: Industrial Gas Solutions
segments.commentary: Won 8 large 1,500 cubic metre cryogenic storage tanks for a global space exploration customer plus 6 repeat tanks; also disposable cylinder repeat orders (crossed 2 million cylinders in FY26) and Cryoseal/liquid cylinder traction with capacity expansion. Semiconductor orders from Dholera were modest (~INR30 crore+ per management in Q&A).

segments.name: LNG Solutions
segments.commentary: Orders from Sabarmati Gas, Ultra Gas and BPCL for LNG fuelling stations and healthy LNG semi-trailer orders. Bahamas mini LNG terminal: first large tanks reached site, installation underway; two more orders for Eleuthera and Great Abaco. Cochin Shipyard marine LNG fuel tank execution continues.

segments.name: Cryo-Scientific Division
segments.commentary: Secured a CERN order for specialised cryogenic modules and another order from ITER France. Management said big LNG and CSD projects are delayed by customer issues and regulatory approvals, expected to materialise in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Beverage Kegs
segments.commentary: Orders from Heineken India, Hartwall Finland, ORBEN Germany and a UK brewery; RFQs from Asahi and CCU Chile. Keg capacity is 300,000 units and is under-utilised; management guides utilisation from ~30% to 50-60% by year-end.

segments.name: Aerospace (new)
segments.commentary: Received AS9100D certification, enabling onboard flight components beyond ground support equipment. Overall US private space order exposure is over INR1,000 crore; management said about INR400 crore of the current order book is aerospace.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20%; management reiterated this on the call, expecting dispatch delays to recover over Q2.
EBITDA margin guided at 21-24%; Q1 at 23.5% is within range.
Q1 revenue was targeted at INR410-415 crore; INR32-35 crore of ready equipment slipped out of the quarter.
Order inflow guidance of INR450-500 crore per quarter; management said it may be revised slightly upward given lumpy orders.
Kandla plant expected to start operations by December end or mid-January. Aerospace order execution to start in Q3/Q4 FY27, mainly completing in FY28.
Industrial gas non-aerospace growth expected around 15-18%. Domestic/export order mix to remain around 60:40.
US market entry not possible before 2028 due to non-compete agreement; preparation underway.
capex_capacity: Savli facility: Cryo shop and keg shop both in full production; long-lead equipment and PEB structures ordered.
Kandla facility: civil work underway, PEB structures and major machines ordered; operations targeted for December end or mid-January.
Keg capacity 300,000 units, currently under-utilised; utilisation expected to rise from ~30% to 50-60% by year-end.
Aerospace space order: deliveries planned by end of FY28 across Kandla and Savli; FY27 on percentage-of-completion basis, FY28 on dispatch.
Wayout water microfactory: first module design complete, 6-8 months of construction and testing planned.
demand_pricing: Record INR532 crore order inflow; management said it is hopeful of more lumpy aerospace and mini LNG orders from the pipeline.
Export order book over INR1,140 crore out of INR1,686 crore total order book.

Q1 dispatches hit by freight costs rising sharply (container to Europe from ~$3-4k to ~$8-9k) and ship availability constraints; most logistics cost sits with customers, some of whom deferred deliveries.
Competition: management named Chart Industries (US) as the only known competitor for large space cryogenic tanks; said stringent eligibility criteria keep smaller entrants out.
Transformer tank business (GE orders) may be discontinued because it is carbon steel fabrication, outside core capability, despite better margins.
LNG demand improving as lower LNG prices widen the gap with diesel; PSU RFQs for about 20-25 fuelling stations.

qa_highlights.question: How much TAM does the new AS9100D certification add in aerospace, and what products?
qa_highlights.answer: Previously qualified only for ground equipment; now eligible to bid on flight projects. Targets include propellant tanks for rockets and an EoI for LVM3 manufacturing; the certification is the first eligibility criterion for flight equipment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18-20% growth guidance intact and is order inflow guidance being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth guidance of 18-20% is intact; order inflow guidance may move up slightly from INR450-500 crore given lumpy orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue below the 18-20% growth guided?
qa_highlights.answer: INR32-35 crore of ready equipment was held back due to logistics and freight issues; management said dispatches should stabilise over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US private space order exposure and its execution profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall order from this customer is over INR1,000 crore; delivery target is end FY28, with percentage-of-completion revenue recognition in FY27 and dispatch-based in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: When will US market entry happen and what is the timeline for LNG and Cryo-Scientific bids?
qa_highlights.answer: US entry not possible before 2028 under the non-compete. Large LNG and CSD projects are delayed by customer and regulatory approvals; management expects them in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the keg utilisation and breakeven status?
qa_highlights.answer: Keg plant has 300,000-unit capacity and is under-utilised; utilisation expected to rise from ~30% to 50-60% by year-end. No breakeven figure given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial timeline for the data centre cooling prototype?
qa_highlights.answer: Production line frozen; prototype development to start after consultant review. Commercialisation at least 1-1.5 years away.

financial_highlights.change: slightly below previous quarter; within 21-24% guided range

risks_watch: Q1 revenue shortfall: INR32-35 crore of ready equipment held back by freight spikes (container to Europe ~$3-4k to ~$8-9k) and ship availability; track whether it dispatches in Q2 as management expects.

Execution concentration: US private space order is over INR1,000 crore, with delivery targeted by end FY28 and about INR400 crore of current order book in aerospace; dispatch-based recognition from FY28 shifts revenue timing.
Delayed LNG and Cryo-Scientific project awards (customer issues, regulatory approvals, geopolitics); management says one to two quarters, so watch for conversion of bids into orders.
Keg utilisation at 300,000-unit capacity is about 30% and guided to 50-60% by year-end; Savli and Kandla start-up costs weigh on margins against the 21-24% EBITDA guide.
Kandla plant start targeted December end or mid-January; any slip would pressure FY27 18-20% growth guidance, which management reiterated as intact.
US market entry not possible before 2028 under non-compete; transformer tank business (GE orders) may be discontinued.
key_quotes: As guided in our previous interactions, we delivered our highest ever quarterly order inflow of approximately INR532 crores, taking our total order book to around INR1,686 crores, the highest in the company's history.
So basically, the revenue we did INR382 crores and we have targeted something around INR410 crores or INR415 crores.

Yes. Savli facility, the recent new facility, we have already started the civil work & we have already ordered all the equipments, which are major long lead equipments, and the Pre-Engineered Building structures is also ordered now.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on guidance and order momentum, reiterating 18-20% FY27 growth and the 21-24% EBITDA range despite the Q1 shortfall. It was more cautious and vague on timing for LNG and Cryo-Scientific projects and on semiconductor order value, and gave no segment EBITDA or breakeven figures.

adds.what: Kandla plant (new facility, civil work underway, PEB structures and major machines ordered)
Keg capacity utilisation ramp to 50-60% at existing 300,000-unit keg capacity (utilisation, not new capacity)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% (midpoint 19%), reiterated, backed by a record INR1,686 crore order book (over INR1,140 crore export) and record INR532 crore Q1 order inflow, plus Kandla plant targeted for December end or mid-January; Q1 revenue grew only 8.3% after INR32-35 crore of ready equipment slipped on freight and ship constraints.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin 23.5% sits inside the 21-24% guide, but Savli and Kandla start-up costs weigh on margins and keg utilisation is only ~30%, with 50-60% guided by year-end, so expansion is conditional on utilisation and dispatch recovery rather than firmly committed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kandla plant has civil work underway with PEB structures and major machines ordered, targeted to start by December end or mid-January; keg capacity of 300,000 units is already in place but only ~30% utilised.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% and reiterated; record INR532 crore Q1 order inflow and INR1,686 crore order book (over INR1,140 crore export) support it, though Q1 revenue grew only 8.3% after INR32-35 crore of ready equipment slipped on freight constraints, and industrial gas non-aerospace growth is guided at 15-18%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management referenced capacity expansion initiatives including Kandla and 'other strategic growth opportunities' and an aerospace space order needing delivery by end FY28, but no new capex amount or size was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order inflow guidance of INR450-500 crore per quarter may be revised slightly upward given lumpy orders, after a record INR532 crore Q1, but revenue and margin guidance were only reiterated, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue of INR382 crore missed management's own INR410-415 crore target by ~INR28-33 crore, and any Kandla slip beyond mid-January or a failure of the INR32-35 crore held-back equipment to dispatch in Q2 would pressure the 18-20% growth guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AS9100D certification enables flight components beyond ground support equipment, with aerospace order execution starting Q3/Q4 FY27 and about INR400 crore of the current order book in aerospace; LNG and Cryo-Scientific projects expected in one to two quarters.

rows.label: Record order book INR1,686 crore with lumpy LNG and aerospace pipeline
rows.why: Order book is at a record INR1,686 crore (over INR1,140 crore export), and management expects big LNG and CSD projects to convert in one to two quarters, though customer and regulatory delays have already slipped timing.

rows.label: Keg utilisation ramp from ~30% to 50-60%
rows.why: Keg capacity of 300,000 units is about 30% utilised with management guiding 50-60% by year-end, which would lift fixed-cost absorption against Savli and Kandla start-up costs.

rows.label: US market entry
rows.why: A non-compete agreement rules out US market entry before 2028, so no US revenue contribution falls inside the next 2-4 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 18-20% FY27 growth guide, 21-24% EBITDA range and record order inflow, but cautious and vague on LNG and Cryo-Scientific timing and semiconductor order value; analysts pressed on the Q1 revenue shortfall against the INR410-415 crore target.
